originality.rationale: Three primary full texts and actual semantic record searches were compared at the level of mixed-query implications. Known four-request simplex and functional-PIR recurrences do not yield six-request arbitrary-query service. The eleven-column six-request block is necessary to close a previously uncovered congruence class, and the resulting ten-request bound improves a published upper bound.
residual_risks: An equivalently strong six-request construction may exist in unindexed coding-theory or parallel-RIO literature.
The finite witnesses and novelty comparisons have not been independently mathematically audited.

value.rationale: A natural all-t exact storage invariant (stronger arbitrary-target batch condition) with a sharp singleton exception, based on a nontrivial complete 924-request certificate. It produces an eighteen-column ten-request functional-batch design, improving on the 2019 table's nineteen-column functional-PIR construction benchmark (without claiming this is the later best PIR bound), and precisely identifies the difficulty of the t=2 congruence class.
